module purpose: This module decodes control fields into supported bit-manipulation operations, latches operand, shift and comparison inputs, runs either direct combinational logic or multi-cycle shift/clmul helpers, and registers the selected result on res_o together with valid_o.

use-case flows.value: decode and accept a supported bit-manipulation request, then choose immediate completion, shifter start, or carry-less-multiply start
capture operand, shift-amount and comparison inputs for the active operation
shift/count/rotate processing, either serial or fast, producing shifter values used for cz/cpop/rot results
carry-less multiply processing and selection of upper or lower result half
combinational bit-manipulation result generation and command-qualified result selection
assert completion and drive the registered result to the output interface
clear controller state, captured inputs, helper state, completion flag and output result

conceptual assets.concept: Decoded and accepted bit-manipulation operation request
conceptual assets.reasoning: Lines 132-161 derive cmd bits from ctrl_i.ir_opcode, ctrl_i.ir_funct12 and ctrl_i.ir_funct3, under the build-time enables EN_ZBA, EN_ZBB, EN_ZBKB, EN_ZBKC and EN_ZBS. Line 164 raises valid_cmd only when ctrl_i.alu_cp_alu='1' and some cmd bit is set. Lines 199-205 use this decision to start shifter.start, start clmul.start, or complete immediately, and lines 461-480 use cmd again to admit only the matching result term into res_out. Integrity is established because corrupting this decoded/accepted request changes both the selected computation and the result path; availability is established for requests that satisfy these predicates while the controller is idle.

conceptual assets.concept: Latched operand and auxiliary input context for the active operation
conceptual assets.reasoning: When ctrl_i.alu_cp_alu='1', lines 188-191 capture cmp_i, rs1_i, rs2_i and shamt_i into less_reg, rs1_reg, rs2_reg and sha_reg. Later logic reads these stored values to initialize or compute results at lines 243, 298, 313-314, 326-334, 360 and 389-456. Integrity is established because wrong captured values make the selected bit-manipulation result wrong, and availability is established because multi-cycle flows rely on these values being preserved until completion.

The controller stores S_IDLE, S_START and S_BUSY in ctrl_state (lines 172, 202, 205, 208, 214, 220). Lines 195-220 branch on ctrl_state to decide whether a new request starts helper engines, whether execution is busy, and when completion returns to idle after shifter/clmul finish or cpu_trap. Integrity is established because corrupting this state changes start, busy and finish sequencing; availability is established because the implemented progress through idle, start and busy depends on these transitions.

With not EN_FAST_SHIFT, lines 241-259 initialize and update shifter.sreg, shifter.cnt, shifter.cnt_max and shifter.bcnt, while lines 266-287 derive the next shift bit and run/stop condition. With EN_FAST_SHIFT, lines 307, 310 and 313-319 compute the same shifter values directly. Lines 395, 399 and 414 move these values into res_int for count-zero, population-count and rotate results, and line 218 waits for shifter.run before reporting completion. Integrity is established because these values define the shift/count result; availability is established because the serial path must preserve and advance this state until completion.

conceptual assets.concept: Carry-less multiply working state and partial result
conceptual assets.reasoning: When EN_ZBKC is enabled, lines 358-368 initialize and update clmul.cnt and clmul.res, line 374 derives clmul.run from the counter, and line 456 selects the upper or lower XLEN half of clmul.res into res_int(op_clmul_c). Line 218 waits for clmul.run to drop before completion is reported. Integrity is established because the carry-less-multiply result depends on this counter and partial-product state; availability is established because completion requires the counter to progress to zero. When EN_ZBKC is false, lines 380-382 tie these elements inactive.

valid is cleared on reset and by default each cycle (lines 179 and 184), set in the immediate-completion path (line 207) or after helper completion or trap (line 219), gates the result update at line 491, and is copied to valid_o at line 502. Integrity is established because wrong assertion or suppression changes when downstream logic may trust res_o; availability is established under the RTL-visible completion conditions that set valid.

Lines 389-456 compute candidate result terms from the captured inputs and helper state. Lines 461-480 qualify those terms with cmd and the build-time enables into res_out. Lines 491-496 then register the OR-combined selected result onto res_o only when valid='1'. Integrity is established because the consumer of this module must receive exactly the result defined by these equations and command qualifiers; availability is established only under the RTL condition that valid is asserted for that operation.
